paragraphs.source_en: It’s been a bit of a trek, but we are now set for the key point. If one does stick to measuring distances “the easy way’—that is, using the lightest of the string modes instead of the heavy ones—the results obtained will always be larger than the Planck length. To see this, let’s think through the hypothetical big crunch for the three extended dimensions, assuming them to be circular. For argument’s sake, let’s say that ai the beginning of our thought experiment, unwound string modes are the light ones and by using them it is determined that the universe has an enormously large radius and that it is shrinking in time. As it shrinks, these unwound modes get heavier and the winding modes get lighter. When the radius shrinks all the way to the Planck length—that is, when R takes on the value 1—the winding and vibration modes have comparable mass.
